examples.ko: 그는 자신의 잘못을 속죄하려고 봉사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: He started volunteering to atone for his mistake.

examples.ko: 어떻게 해야 이 죄를 속죄할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: What do I have to do to atone for this sin?
He said he would live atoning for it for the rest of his life.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 이미 충분히 속죄했다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think that person has already atoned enough.
The way to atone for a wrong is different for each person.
Even if you atone, what happened doesn't disappear.

explain: '잘못을 속죄하다', '죄를 속죄하다'처럼 잘못이나 죄를 목적어로 써요. 말로 '사과하다'가 아니라 행동이나 대가로 갚는 느낌이 있고, 일상 대화보다 글, 영화, 종교 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I donate every month with a heart of atonement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 갚으려는 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for the wish to make up for a wrong.

phrases.en: I want to atone for my mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갚고 싶은 바람을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to express a wish to make up for something.

phrases.en: He lived his whole life atoning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 계속 갚으며 산다는 뜻의 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form meaning to live while continuing to atone for a long time.

explain_en: It takes a wrong or sin as its object, as in '잘못을 속죄하다' or '죄를 속죄하다'. Unlike '사과하다' (to apologize in words), it suggests paying back through actions or a price, and it appears more in writing, films and religious talk than in daily speech.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 집을 살 요량으로 돈을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving money with the intention of buying a house this year.

examples.ko: 그냥 잠깐 쉴 요량이었는데 깜빡 잠들었어요.
examples.en: I only meant to rest for a moment, but I dozed off.

examples.ko: 도대체 어떤 요량으로 그런 말을 했는지 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I have no idea what he was thinking when he said that.
I'm planning to clean this weekend.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 혼자 다 할 요량인가 봐요.
examples.en: It seems he intends to do it all by himself.

examples.ko: 아무 요량도 없이 일을 시작하면 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you start a job with no plan at all, it gets hard.

explain: 거의 '-ㄹ 요량으로', '-ㄹ 요량이다' 꼴로 써요. '-ㄹ 생각으로', '-ㄹ 셈으로'와 비슷하지만 속으로 정해 둔 계획이나 속셈이라는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요. 대화보다 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 휴가 때 여행을 갈 요량으로 비행기 표를 알아봤어요.
phrases.en: I looked up plane tickets intending to travel during my vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 하려는 속마음을 말하며 뒤에 하는 행동을 이어 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: States your inner intention and connects it to the action that follows.

phrases.example: 저는 이번 주말에 푹 쉴 요량이에요.
phrases.en: I'm planning to get a good rest this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장을 끝낼 때 쓰며, 마음속으로 정해 둔 계획을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to end a sentence, stating a plan you have decided in your mind.

phrases.example: 그 일을 오늘 끝낼 셈으로 밤을 새웠어요.
phrases.en: I stayed up all night intending to finish that work today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요량으로'와 비슷하지만 대화에서도 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'yoryang-euro', but used more often in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is used almost only in the forms '-ㄹ 요량으로' and '-ㄹ 요량이다'. It is close to '-ㄹ 생각으로' or '-ㄹ 셈으로', but suggests a plan or private intention you have worked out inside. It shows up more in writing and storytelling than in casual talk.

t90.ax: I'm planning to clean this weekend.

en: to be ambitious; to be lofty; to be grand

examples.en: Our company set a grand goal.
The dream is so grand that I want to cheer for it.
This plan is more far-reaching than I thought.

examples.ko: 원대하게 시작했지만 끝까지 가기는 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: We started on a grand scale, but it was not easy to carry it to the end.

examples.ko: 목표가 원대할수록 작은 준비부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: The grander the goal, the more you should start with small preparations.
It does not have to be grand, so keep at it steadily.

explain: 꿈, 계획, 포부, 목표 같은 말과 함께 써요. 사람이나 물건의 크기에는 쓰지 않고, 규모가 크고 앞날이 멀다는 점을 높이 보는 느낌이에요. 일상에서는 '큰 꿈'이라고 해도 돼요. 반대 느낌으로는 '소박하다'를 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 도시를 바꿀 원대한 계획을 세웠어요.
phrases.en: He made a grand plan to change the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규모가 크고 앞날이 먼 계획에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for large plans that look far ahead.

phrases.en: The new employee spoke of lofty ambitions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속의 큰 뜻을 말할 때 '포부'와 짝을 이뤄요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '포부' for big hopes in one's heart.

phrases.en: My dream isn't grand, but I'm happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 소박한 꿈을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can describe a modest dream.

explain_en: Describes dreams or plans as large and lofty, positive (원대한 꿈) It goes with words like 꿈 (dream), 계획 (plan), 포부 (aspiration) and 목표 (goal). It is not used for the physical size of people or things; it praises a large scale and a distant future. In daily talk 큰 꿈 works too. 소박하다 gives the opposite feel.

t90.ax: Our company set a grand goal.

examples.en: He accepted even the hard verdict calmly.
My mother got up firmly and looked after the children.
You have to face a crisis with composure.
Even after losing, the player greeted everyone with composure.

examples.ko: 의연히 앞을 보며 걸어가는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The way he walked on, looking steadily ahead, was cool.

examples.ko: 오랜 세월이 지나도 마을 입구의 나무는 의연히 그대로예요.
examples.en: Even after many years, the tree at the village entrance remains just as it was.

explain: 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 쓰고, 말할 때는 '의연하게'가 더 자연스러워요. 침착하고 흔들림 없이라는 뜻 외에, 예문처럼 '예전과 다름없이'라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: He smiled calmly even in the face of failure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '의연히'보다 이 형태가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form sounds more natural than 의연히 in speech.

phrases.en: The residents faced the difficulties firmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 뉴스에서 어려움과 마주할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing and news for facing hardship.

phrases.example: 오래된 나무가 마을 입구에 의연히 서 있어요.
phrases.en: The old tree stands steadfast at the village entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변함없이 그대로 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something staying as it always has.

explain_en: It is mostly used in writing or news, and '의연하게' sounds more natural in speech. Besides 'calmly and without wavering', it can also mean 'just as before', as in the last example.

examples.en: Right now I desperately need a rest.
He was in a situation where he badly needed money.
I earnestly hoped to pass.
At that moment I felt keenly how much I needed help.

examples.ko: 선생님이 해 주신 말이 절실히 와닿았어요.
examples.en: What my teacher said really hit home.

examples.ko: 난민들은 음식과 물을 절실히 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: The refugees are anxiously waiting for food and water.

explain: '필요하다', '바라다', '느끼다', '와닿다'와 잘 어울려요. '정말', '매우'보다 마음이 급하고 간절한 느낌이 강해요. 형용사 '절실하다'에서 온 부사예요.

phrases.en: I earnestly hope that my whole family stays healthy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절실히'를 '바라다'와 함께 쓰면 마음속 소원이 아주 간절하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 바라다, it expresses a deeply felt, earnest wish.

phrases.en: I keenly felt how precious health is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 겪고 나서 깊이 깨달았을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when you deeply realize something after experiencing it.

phrases.en: I wished earnestly to pass.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절실히'와 비슷하지만 '간절히'는 마음을 다해 바라는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 절실히, but with a stronger sense of wishing with all your heart.

explain_en: It pairs well with '필요하다', '바라다', '느끼다' and '와닿다'. It feels more urgent and heartfelt than '정말' or '매우'. It is the adverb form of the adjective '절실하다'.

examples.ko: 화가 날 때는 감정을 제어하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to control your emotions when you're angry.
I control the lights at home with my smartphone.
The driver couldn't control the speed.
I'm making a program that controls a robot.

examples.ko: 식욕을 제어할 수 있는 방법이 있을까요?
examples.en: Is there a way to keep your appetite in check?
After getting the flames under control, they checked for safety.

explain: '조절하다'와 '다스리다'의 중간 느낌으로, 움직임이나 상태를 원하는 대로 다룰 때 써요. 기계나 시스템뿐 아니라 감정·욕구에도 쓰고, 사람을 억지로 누르는 건 '통제하다'가 맞아요. 멀리서 기계를 움직이는 건 '원격 제어'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I couldn't control my anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 상황을 다스리지 못했을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when one couldn't keep feelings or a situation in check.

phrases.en: Please adjust the air conditioner's temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제어하다'보다 쉬운 말이고 알맞게 맞춘다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word with the feel of setting something to a suitable level.

phrases.en: I control the robot remotely with an app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멀리서 기계를 움직일 때 '원격으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '원격으로' when operating a machine from far away.

explain_en: Technical control of machines or systems; formal, written. Between '조절하다' (adjust) and '다스리다' (govern): handling movement or condition as you want. It applies to machines and systems as well as emotions and urges. Forcing people down is '통제하다'. Operating a machine from a distance is '원격 제어'.

dis.h: control a machine or system technically
gh: handle one's own feelings; mostly negated
loanword; control skill, emotions, or ball

p.n: 컨트롤하다 is the same idea, but a more casual loanword.

t90.ax: The driver couldn't control the speed.

en: to squeeze out; to wring out; to come up with

examples.ko: 치약을 끝까지 짜낸 다음에 새것을 샀어요.
examples.en: I squeezed out the toothpaste to the end and then bought a new one.
Squeeze the lemon and put it in the water.
I wring the water out of the wet clothes.
I stayed up all night squeezing out ideas.

examples.ko: 회의에서 좋은 방법을 짜내 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: At the meeting, they said let's come up with a good method.
I'm worried because there's no way to scrape money together.

explain: '짜다'는 눌러서 물이나 내용물을 나오게 하는 말이고, '짜내다'는 끝까지 힘을 줘서 밖으로 빼내는 느낌이 더 강해요. 아이디어나 돈처럼 어렵게 만들어 낼 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I racked my brain to solve the problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 열심히 생각해서 방법을 찾으려고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you think very hard to find a way.

explain_en: Press so contents come out (치약, 즙) 짜다 means pressing to get liquid or contents out; 짜내다 feels stronger, as if you push until it all comes out. It is also used for producing things with effort, like ideas or money.

t90.ax: I wring the water out of the wet clothes.

examples.en: We converted an old warehouse into a cafe.
You need permission if you want to modify a car.
It's a bicycle my father modified himself.

examples.ko: 집을 개조하는 동안 친구 집에서 지냈어요.
examples.en: I stayed at a friend's house while the house was being remodeled.
They plan to convert this building into a hotel.

examples.ko: 방을 개조하고 나니 훨씬 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: After remodeling the room, it looks much bigger.

explain: 건물, 차, 기계의 구조를 바꾸어서 다른 용도로 만들 때 써요. '고치다'는 고장 난 것을 원래대로 돌리는 일이고, '개조하다'는 원래와 다르게 바꾸는 일이에요. 인테리어를 조금 바꾸는 정도는 '리모델링'이라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The old bus was converted into a food truck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀌는 물건을 중심으로 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the thing that is changed.

phrases.en: I modified an old desk and I'm using it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 모양을 바꿔서 다른 용도로 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means changing the original form and using it for another purpose.

phrases.en: We remodeled the bathroom this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 안을 조금 새롭게 꾸밀 때는 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used more often for giving a home's interior a fresh update.

explain_en: Use it when you change the structure of a building, car or machine to give it a new use. 고치다 means fixing something back to how it was; 개조하다 means changing it into something different. For smaller interior updates, Koreans often say 리모델링.

examples.ko: 우리 집 인터넷은 광섬유로 연결돼 있어요.
examples.en: The internet at my home is connected by optical fiber.

examples.ko: 광섬유는 빛으로 정보를 전달해서 속도가 빨라요.
examples.en: Optical fiber carries information as light, so it is fast.

examples.ko: 바다 밑에 광섬유 케이블이 깔려 있대요.
examples.en: I heard optical fiber cables are laid under the sea.

examples.ko: 의사들은 광섬유를 이용한 내시경으로 몸속을 살펴봐요.
examples.en: Doctors examine the inside of the body with an endoscope that uses optical fiber.

examples.ko: 광섬유가 끊어져서 인터넷이 한참 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The optical fiber was cut, so the internet was down for a long while.

examples.ko: 광섬유처럼 가는 줄이 빛을 따라 반짝였어요.
examples.en: A thin line like optical fiber sparkled with the light.

explain: 빛을 통과시키는 아주 가는 유리나 플라스틱 섬유예요. 이것으로 만든 통신선은 '광케이블'이라고도 불러요. 인터넷 속도 이야기를 할 때 '광랜'이나 '광통신'과 같이 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: They laid optical fiber cables under the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통신선을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about communication lines.

phrases.en: Fiber cable comes into our building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광섬유'로 만든 통신선을 줄여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter name for communication lines made of optical fiber.

phrases.en: Optical communication sends signals with light.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광섬유를 이용한 통신 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to communication that uses optical fiber.

explain_en: It is a very thin glass or plastic fiber that carries light. A communication line made from it is also called '광케이블' (optical cable). You often meet it in talk about internet speed, alongside words like '광랜' and '광통신'.

examples.ko: 에어컨 냉매가 새면 시원한 바람이 잘 안 나와요.
examples.en: If the air conditioner's refrigerant leaks, the cool air doesn't come out well.

examples.ko: 냉매를 새로 채우는 데 돈이 얼마나 들까요?
examples.en: How much would it cost to refill the refrigerant?
There is refrigerant inside a refrigerator too.

examples.ko: 냉매가 부족한 것 같으니 기사님을 부르세요.
examples.en: It seems the refrigerant is low, so call a technician.

examples.ko: 이 에어컨은 환경에 덜 해로운 냉매를 써요.
examples.en: This air conditioner uses a refrigerant that is less harmful to the environment.

examples.ko: 냉매 가스를 함부로 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not dispose of refrigerant gas carelessly.

explain: 에어컨이나 냉장고 안에서 열을 옮겨 차갑게 만들어 주는 물질이에요. 고장 수리 이야기에서 '냉매가 새다', '냉매를 채우다'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 냉장고에서 냉매가 새서 수리 기사님을 불렀어요.
phrases.en: The refrigerant was leaking from the fridge, so I called a repair technician.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고장 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most frequent collocation in talk about breakdowns.

phrases.en: The technician refilled the air conditioner with refrigerant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수리할 때 냉매를 새로 넣는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to putting in new refrigerant during a repair.

phrases.en: Refrigerant gas is dangerous to handle carelessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉매가 기체 상태일 때를 말하며 안전 안내에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to refrigerant in gas form; often seen in safety notices.

explain_en: It is the substance inside air conditioners and refrigerators that moves heat to make things cold. In repair talk you hear phrases like '냉매가 새다' and '냉매를 채우다'.

examples.en: I drew water up from the well with a bucket.
The bucket was so heavy that I pulled it up with all my strength.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 마당에는 오래된 우물과 두레박이 있어요.
examples.en: In Grandpa's yard there is an old well and a well bucket.
When I dropped the bucket, there was a splash.

examples.ko: 민속촌에서 두레박으로 물 긷는 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: I tried drawing water with a well bucket at the folk village.

examples.ko: 두레박 줄이 짧아서 물이 닿지 않았어요.
examples.en: The bucket rope was short, so it didn't reach the water.

explain: 우물물을 줄로 내려 퍼 올리는 그릇이에요. 지금은 옛이야기, 동화, 민속촌에서 주로 만나요. 물을 '긷다'는 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '길어요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Grandmother drew water with a well bucket.
phrases.nuance_ko: '긷다'는 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '길으셨어요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 긷다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb, so it changes to 길으셨어요.
phrases.en_equiv: to draw water with a bucket

phrases.en: I lowered the bucket into the well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 푸기 전에 줄을 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you lower the rope before drawing water.

phrases.en: The bucket rope is too short.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두레박에 달린 줄을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the rope attached to the bucket.

explain_en: It is a bucket lowered on a rope to scoop water from a well. Today you mostly meet it in old tales, fairy tales and folk villages. The verb for drawing water, '긷다', is a ㄷ-irregular verb and becomes '길어요'.

examples.ko: 화분에 꽃을 옮겨 심을 때 모종삽을 써요.
examples.en: I use a trowel when I transplant flowers into a pot.
I dug the soil with a trowel in my balcony garden.
The trowel is small, so even a child can use it easily.
I bought a trowel at the flower shop.
Where did you put the trowel we were using earlier?

examples.ko: 모종삽 끝으로 흙을 살짝 파고 모종을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I dug a little soil with the tip of the trowel and put in the seedling.

explain: '모종'은 옮겨 심는 어린 식물이고, 모종삽은 그걸 심을 때 쓰는 작은 삽이에요. 일반 '삽'보다 훨씬 작아서 화분이나 텃밭 가꿀 때 써요.

phrases.en: I dug the soil with a trowel to make a hole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구로 쓰는 '-(으)로'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic use, with -(으)로 marking the tool.
phrases.en_equiv: to dig soil with a trowel

phrases.example: 화분에 심을 때는 모종삽을 쓰면 편해요.
phrases.en: A trowel is handy for planting in pots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 사용한다는 뜻으로 간단히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to say you use the tool.

phrases.en: I bought seedlings and a trowel together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모종삽은 모종을 심는 도구라서 두 말이 함께 나오는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words often appear together since the trowel is for planting seedlings.

explain_en: '모종' is a young plant for transplanting, and a 모종삽 is the small shovel for planting it. It is much smaller than an ordinary '삽', and is used for pots and small vegetable gardens.

examples.ko: 과일 세척제를 써서 농약을 씻어 냈어요.
examples.en: I used a fruit wash to rinse off the pesticide.

examples.ko: 세척제는 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep the cleaning product out of children's reach.
This cleaner works well on greasy stains.
I bought a new bathroom cleaner.

examples.ko: 세척제를 너무 많이 쓰면 헹구기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you use too much cleaner, it's hard to rinse off.
I wash the baby bottles with bottle cleanser.

explain: '세제'가 빨래나 설거지처럼 넓게 쓰는 말이라면 '세척제'는 과일, 젖병, 욕실, 기계처럼 씻어 내는 대상에 맞춘 제품에 많이 붙여요. 제품 이름이나 설명에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I cleaned the tiles with a bathroom cleaner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 욕실의 물때나 곰팡이를 닦는 제품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A product for removing limescale and mold in the bathroom.

phrases.en: I bought a baby-safe bottle cleaner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기용품을 씻는 제품에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly seen on products for washing baby items.

phrases.en: I sprayed cleaner on the stain and wiped it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세척제를 실제로 쓰는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of actually using the cleaner.

explain_en: While '세제' is a broad word for laundry or dish detergent, '세척제' is often attached to products made for a specific target, such as fruit, baby bottles, bathrooms or machines. You often see it in product names and descriptions.

examples.en: Even the country house now has a flush toilet.
It used to be very inconvenient because it wasn't a flush toilet.
The campsite restroom was clean because it had flush toilets.
The flush toilet got clogged, so I called someone.
My grandmother's house still doesn't have a flush toilet.

examples.ko: 수세식으로 바꾸는 공사를 다음 달에 해요.
examples.en: The work to switch to a flush toilet is next month.

explain: 보통 '수세식 화장실', '수세식 변기'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 물로 씻어 내리지 않는 옛날 방식은 '재래식 화장실'이라고 해서 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 요즘은 거의 모든 집에 수세식 화장실이 있어요.
phrases.en: These days almost every home has a flush toilet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 물로 씻어 내리는 화장실을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing; a toilet that flushes with water.

phrases.example: 수세식 변기가 고장 나서 사람을 불렀어요.
phrases.en: The flush toilet broke, so I called a repairman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장실 전체가 아니라 변기 물건 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the toilet fixture itself, not the whole room.

explain_en: It is usually placed before a noun, as in '수세식 화장실' or '수세식 변기'. The old-style toilet without flushing is called '재래식 화장실', so it helps to remember the two as a pair.
